claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not In-Source in this compilation, including diagnostics created with a null/Location.None location. Existing diagnostics with no location (e.g. ones built with GetIdentifierLocation returning null, or other call sites) and diagnostics located in other syntax trees in the same compilation behave differently, so users who previously saw MsgPack00x diagnostics (possibly errors) may no longer get them. This is a global behavior change beyond the three crash sites.

claim: The constructor now wraps every analyzer diagnostic in `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`. That drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the compilation, including diagnostics about source-declared types. Several helpers (`GetLocation(IParameterSymbol)`, `GetParameterListLocation`, `GetIdentifierLocation`, and the new `FirstOrDefault()` at line 1077) return null for implicitly declared symbols, which yields `Location.None`. Such diagnostics were reported before and are now silently suppressed. Examples are an implicit or primary constructor, or compiler-synthesized record members in the compiling project. This conflicts with the criterion that types declared in the same assembly keep working as before.

claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` drops every diagnostic whose `Location` is not `IsInSource`, including `Location.None`. That is broader than metadata symbols. Two cases where the formatted type itself is in the compilation now lose their diagnostics: (a) a location helper returns null (`GetParameterListLocation`/`GetLocation` on an implicitly declared constructor or synthesized parameter); (b) the offending member is inherited from a base class in a referenced assembly (e.g. MsgPack004 for an unkeyed public property of a metadata base). The analyzer stays silent, while the generator still skips or fails that member or formatter. The remark says the defining compilation reports these, which is false for a source type.
